messages.subject: GIGAMUGA mapping issues
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I followed the guide for preparing DO mouse data for qtl2 for my GIGAMUGA data (http://kbroman.org/qtl2/pages/prep_do_data.html), but I've been getting strange issues after mapping.

Upon calculating QTL effects with scan1coef(), I've noticed that certain chromosomes return very strange results (refer to chrom1.png), while other chromosomes return more typical-looking results (chrom2.png)

When I looked at the range of values for the 6th allele in my scan1coef() object for chromosome 1, I noted the following strange results:

> range(na.omit(coef_c2[,6]))
[1] -172696229324     249156537

while the "real" range is the following:

> range(na.omit(coef_c2[,5]))
[1] 1.592147 4.778550

This error seems to occur in chromosomes 2,5,6,8,11,13,14,15,16,18 and X, and as far as I can tell, is not restricted to the 6th allele.

Any help would be appreciated.

-Basel Al-Barghouthi

messages.body_plain:

On other chromosomes, all alleles are present in the full 192 mice, but when you reduce to 56 mice, there'll be alleles missing from those 56 at particular positions.

karl

I wasn't able to find anything obviously wrong with the data. With 192 mice, it shouldn't be a surprise to find some regions with missing alleles. And when you reduce to ~60 mice for some phenotypes, there will be loads of such places.

And you can potentially obtain good evidence for genotype:phenotype association even if some of the possible genotypes were not observed.

messages.subject: haplotype reconstruction summary data
messages.body_plain: Is there a way to summarize/visualize the basic haplotype reconstructions for all mice.  For example, it would be nice to see an analysis/graph of some sort that summarizes all of those haplotype reconstructions to show what founder contributions exist across the entire genome in a DO cohort (basically something to show that equal founder contribution was maintained in the xth generation DO cohort that was used).

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] haplotype reconstruction summary data
messages.body_plain:
> Is there a way to summarize/visualize the basic haplotype reconstructions for all mice.  For example, it would be nice to see an analysis/graph of some sort that summarizes all of those haplotype reconstructions to show what founder contributions exist across the entire genome in a DO cohort (basically something to show that equal founder contribution was maintained in the xth generation DO cohort that was used).

I'm working on a tutorial on data diagnostics in multiparent populations such as the DO, but it's been slow going and probably won't be done until late spring.

My basic approach is

1. Verify mouse sex, principally be looking at probe intensities for SNPs on X and Y chromosome. The proportion of heterozygous genotypes on the X is also informative.

2. Look for sample duplicates, by counting the proportion of SNPs with matching genotypes for each pair of samples.

3. Look at the proportion of missing genotypes for each sample, as a way to identify poorly behaved samples. The distribution of SNP array intensities also seems a useful guide.

4. Look at estimated counts of crossovers across the genome.

But you were interested particularly in allele frequencies across the genome. The function calc_geno_freq() is useful for this. You can use either the results of calc_genoprob (with all 36 genotypes), or the allele dosages from genoprob_to_alleleprob().

If you want to look at the genotype reconstructions for individuals, you can use

   plot_genoprob() - heatmap of genotype probabilities for a single individual on a single chromosome
   plot_onegeno() - genome-wide inferred genotypes for a single individual, after first using maxmarg()
                    to infer genotypes and guess_phase() to guess the haplotypes

I paste some example code, below.

karl

--------

# Example with the DOex data (https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/tree/master/DOex)

library(qtl2)
file <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rqtl/",
               "qtl2data/master/DOex/DOex.zip")
DOex <- read_cross2(file)

# genoprobs
pr <- calc_genoprob(DOex, error_prob=0.002)

# allele probs
apr <- genoprob_to_alleleprob(pr)

# histograms of allele frequencies across individuals
af_ind <- calc_geno_freq(apr, "individual")
par(mfrow=c(4,2))
for(i in 1:8) hist(af[,i], main=colnames(af)[i], breaks=30)

# plots of allele frequencies across the genome
af_mar <- calc_geno_freq(apr, "marker", omit_x=FALSE)
plot_coefCC(af_mar, DOex$pmap, ylim=c(0, max(af_mar)), ylab="Allele frequency")

# heatmap of genotype probabilities for a single individual on one chromosome
plot_genoprob(pr, DOex$pmap, chr="2", ind=1, threshold=1/8)

# plot of a single individual's inferred genotypes
### first infer genotypes
m <- maxmarg(pr)
### then guess phase (so we can look at the two haplotypes
v <- guess_phase(DOex, m)
### now the plot
plot_onegeno(v, DOex$pmap, ind=1) # a male
plot_onegeno(v, DOex$pmap, ind=53) # a female
